title: Visual Mechanism Reconstruction Experiment Receipt
description:
Canonical post-execution evidence contract for the Visual Mechanism Reconstruction System. A receipt records what was intended, what actually ran, the exact inputs and outputs, what the results do and do not establish, which failures or deviations occurred, what downstream work may trust, and whether a milestone is unlocked. It is deliberately stricter than a run log: a syntactically valid receipt can still declare itself incomplete or invalid, but it may not claim completion, support, reproducibility, canonical consequence, or milestone unlock without the corresponding evidence and governance gates.

ADVANCED DEFINITION OF DONE
A receipt is done only when: (1) it is bound to an immutable pre-run contract and uniquely identified execution; (2) all authoritative inputs, material configuration, software, hardware, random state, and lineage needed to identify or reproduce the run are recorded; (3) planned and actual actions are distinguishable and every material divergence is classified; (4) expected and actual outputs are enumerated, integrity-addressed where persisted, and checked; (5) every determination states its scope, evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, falsifiers, limitations, and prohibited inferences; (6) tested and supported claims point to executed tests and admissible evidence; (7) timing and measurement applicability are explicitly decided rather than silently omitted; (8) semantic checks prevent observations, interpretations, hypotheses, measurements, and causal claims from being conflated; (9) exceptions, stop conditions, unresolved risks, and scope exclusions are visible; (10) reproducibility is either verified with an independent rerun or honestly classified at a lower state with blockers; (11) canonical changes are separately reviewed, reversible, and never inferred merely from support; (12) the next milestone is unlocked only when its named prerequisites have passed; (13) the handoff states exactly what the next stage may trust, must verify, must not infer, and must receive; and (14) a final validity assessment identifies all conditions that make the receipt incomplete or invalid. The expected output is a self-contained, machine-valid, evidence-linked receipt whose claims can be audited without rerunning the experiment and whose reproduction package makes rerunning possible when required.
$comment: Normative schema. Custom x-* annotations document the recursive Socratic design review and may be ignored by standard JSON Schema validators.

questions_applied_to_every_material_fiel: What downstream decision does this field enable?
What failure or ambiguity does it prevent?
What evidence could falsify or contradict the assertion?
What must the next stage be able to trust without repeating this work?
What omission, contradiction, or unmet condition makes the receipt incomplete or invalid?
x-socratic-method.recursion_rule: Apply the five questions first to the receipt, then to every claim-bearing section, then to each determination, measurement, exception, deviation, governance action, milestone gate, and handoff assertion. Stop refining only when the enabled decision, prevented failure, falsifier, downstream trust boundary, and invalidity condition are explicit or intentionally not applicable with a reason.

invalid_if: A persisted authoritative artifact lacks an integrity digest.
A tested or supported determination lacks an executed test, admissible evidence, and a falsification assessment.
A supported determination omits alternatives, residual uncertainty, limitations, or prohibited inferences.
A canonical state is claimed without approved independent review and explicit canonical consequences.
A milestone is marked unlocked while any named prerequisite is unmet or any blocking stop condition is triggered.
A deviation or exception is known but unrecorded, or its impact on validity is undecided.
Measurement or timing is silently omitted instead of being declared applicable, not applicable, or unknown.
The next stage cannot identify what it may trust, what it must verify, or what it must not infer.
The receipt claims complete while its final validity assessment is incomplete or invalid.

schema_version.description: Version of this receipt contract, enabling deterministic validator and migration selection.

receipt_id.description: Globally stable identifier for this receipt; prevents runs from being confused, overwritten, or merged.

receipt_status.description: Lifecycle state of the receipt document, not the outcome of the experiment. Only complete may unlock a milestone or authorize a canonical change.

supersedes_receipt_id.description: Earlier receipt replaced by this one. The earlier record remains immutable and traceable.

inputs.description: Exact evidence, code, configuration, models, schemas, and prior records consumed by the run.

outputs.description: Expected and actual products of execution, including missing or rejected products so absence cannot disappear from the record.

determinations.description: Bounded conclusions actually licensed by the execution. These are not free-form summaries and do not themselves change canonical knowledge.

alternative_hypotheses.description: Live, weakened, rejected, or newly discovered rival explanations. An empty array is allowed only when the receipt explains in uncertainty why no credible alternative exists.

signed_attestations.description: Optional cryptographic or accountable human/agent attestations. Signatures do not replace evidence or QA.

digest.description: Content digest used to prove artifact identity rather than relying on a mutable name or location.

oneOf.description: Allowed only for ephemeral or missing artifacts, with an explicit integrity limitation.

metadata.description: Artifact-specific descriptive metadata. It must not carry normative claims that belong elsewhere in the receipt.

experimentIdentity.description: Binds the post-run receipt to the pre-run intent and to one concrete attempt, preventing hindsight edits from masquerading as the original plan.

anti_questions.description: Questions the experiment is explicitly not allowed to answer from its evidence.

handoff.description: The explicit trust boundary between stages. It prevents downstream consumers from having to rediscover completed work while forbidding them from silently extending claims beyond the receipt.
